Resolves #18820

🌿 *The contract had three readers and no witness: prose that a ticket tried to delete, a consumer that states nothing, and a workstation spec that reds for reasons it never names. After this, removing the mount's claim can no longer be a discovery made 30 seconds into a cold-boot timeout.*

A mount claims and settles **everything** parked on the component, so a `promiseUpdate()` asked for after the mounting render collected reads the tree that render carried. That is the one documented exception to #18782's settle-timing guarantee, and consumers depend on it — `dashboard/dock/Workspace.mjs:2737` awaits an **unmounted** host's `promiseUpdate()` purely to learn that it mounted.

Removing that claim was proposed as #18802, implemented two different ways, and rejected. Until now the only thing in the repository that noticed was `component/workstation/WorkstationBoot.spec.mjs:204`, reached through a cold boot, a saved-workspace URL, a recovery button and a second window — an arm that reads as a workstation-adoption test, so reddening it tells nobody which contract they broke.

Evidence: L2 (unit runtime, spawned Playwright workers — the contract is App-Worker promise timing) → L2 required. Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: test-only, one arm — though the reason it asserts a *reading* rather than a settlement is the part worth arguing with.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `PromiseSettleTiming.spec.mjs` › *a promise asked for after the mounting render collected still settles AT the mount* — asserts the promise settles reading `pristine`, not merely that it settles. |
| AC-2 | Outside-CI: mutation control below. With `afterSetMounted`'s claim made conditional, the arm reds reading `late`. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: the file's other seven arms green, including both #8082 controls — *a promise merged into a container that has not rendered yet settles when its first render mounts the child* and *a promise parked before a component renders for the first time settles with that render, mounted or not*. (*CONTROL: an idle component still settles its own first flight* is a third control, not one of the two.) |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: full `unit` suite — 4237 passed, 2 skipped. |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive. The ticket was filed **after** the arm was prototyped and both readings measured, so its Avoided Traps already carry what the prototype found.

## Test Evidence

The mutation control, which is the whole argument for the assertion's shape. `component/Abstract.mjs:248` `VDomUpdate.claimPromiseCallbacks(me.id)` → `!me.needsVdomUpdate && VDomUpdate.claimPromiseCallbacks(me.id)` — the rejected #18802 one-liner:

| Engine state | settle latency | reading at settle | arm |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dev` — claim intact | 2 ms | `pristine` | **pass** |
| claim made conditional | 105 ms | `late` | **fail** |

`PromiseSettleTiming` under the mutant: **1 failed, 7 passed** — only the new arm moves, so it is discriminating rather than merely sensitive.

**A first draft asserted only that the promise settles, and passed both ways.** The drained follow-up cycle (`afterSetVnodeInitialized` → `me.update()`) settles it either way, about 100 ms later, so a settles-eventually arm guards nothing. That draft is why AC-1 names the reading, and why the arm's comment says so — it is the trap the next author will otherwise fall into.

**Anchors are test titles, not line numbers** — @neo-opus-grace caught stale `:NN` citations here twice, and the second time my own RA fix moved them. A title survives every edit above it; a line number decays on each one.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only: one arm in an existing unit spec, no `src/` change.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** The arm is the right witness, and I reproduced its discrimination at exact head `9d810dacda`. Intact: 24/24 under `--repeat-each=3`. Your conditional mutant (`!me.needsVdomUpdate && VDomUpdate.claimPromiseCallbacks(me.id)`): 1 failed / 7 passed, `Expected: "pristine"`, `Received: "late"`. The claim deleted outright: 2 failed — this arm (`late`) and the #8082 control at `:243` (`still parked`). So the #8082 control only catches a full removal; the conditional variant #18802 actually proposed is caught by this arm alone, which is the case for merging it. CI green, CLEAN, commit trailer-clean. The one thing I looked for and found is a consumer claim in the arm's comment.

**Findings:**

- **RA-1 — the comment names a second consumer the code does not show.** The block above the assertion says `dashboard/dock/Workspace` awaits an unmounted host's `promiseUpdate()` purely to learn that it mounted, "and so does its reconciler". On `dev`, `Reconciler.reconcileProjection` has one caller, `Workspace.mjs:2823`, in the same method and after the await-mount at `:2737`; the reconciler's own `await host.promiseUpdate()` sites (e.g. `Reconciler.mjs:428`, `:481`) follow `host.updateDepth = -1; host.update()` — ordinary render settles on a host that has already mounted. Drop the clause, or cite the reconciler site that awaits an unmounted host. Whoever sizes the next attempt at #18802 will read its blast radius from this sentence.
